certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Structural Plywood manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, or selling uncertified structural-grade plywood in the domestic market is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted specific phased transition periods, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to wood panels.
requirements: Every structural plywood panel must be legibly and indelibly marked on its face or edge with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's name or trademark, grade, thickness, type, and licence number (CM/L).

Veneers must be peeled from timbers of specified hardwood species (Annex B) with high natural durability. Only BWP-grade synthetic resin adhesives conforming to IS 848 must be used to ensure water-proof covalent bonding.

Plywood is classified into three structural types based on composition: a) Type 1 (CS): Structural Plywood with core and face veneers of the same species; b) Type 2 (CSC): Structural Plywood with core of one species and face veneers of other species; c) Type 3 (CSFF): Structural Plywood Film Faced (phenolic film-faced).
Core and face veneers must undergo deep chemical vacuum-pressure impregnation (typically CCB or copper naphthenate) to ensure the entire panel is 100% borer, fungus, and termite proof.
Finished structural plywood boards must be seasoned to maintain a uniform moisture content within the range of 5 to 15 percent when tested per IS 1734 (Part 1).
When tested in the dry state per IS 1734 (Part 4), the panel must develop high adhesion strength: a) Average failing load: minimum 1350 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 1100 N.

After 72 hours of continuous boiling water immersion (to simulate extreme weather stress), the panel must satisfy: a) Average failing load: minimum 1000 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 800 N; c) Adhesion of plies (Knife Test): Pass.
The panel must resist fungal attacks. After mycological conditioning, the glue lines must satisfy: a) Average failing load: minimum 1000 N; b) Minimum individual failing load: minimum 800 N.

Along the face grain (parallel), the structural plywood must develop high load-bearing capacity: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 50 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 45 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 7500 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 6700 N/mm².

Across the face grain (perpendicular), the structural plywood must meet: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 30 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 27 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 4000 N/mm², Minimum individual 3600 N/mm².
The structural panel must offer exceptional grip: a) Screw holding strength: minimum 1600 N; b) Nail holding strength: minimum 1300 N.

All boards of the identical thickness and size dispatched against one dispatch note constitute a lot. Random samples must be selected as per Table 3 to perform visual, dimensional, and physical-mechanical testing.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all uncoated stress relieved low relaxation seven-wire strands for prestressed concrete must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial wire/strand products as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Every coil or bundle of strands conforming to the quality and performance requirements of this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) stamped permanently on a secure metal tag attached to the coil.

Strands must be designated according to nominal diameter, nominal tensile strength, and strand type: P for plain, I for indented, and C for compacted. For example, '12.7-1860-I' represents a 12.7 mm nominal diameter indented strand with 1860 MPa tensile strength.

Strand dimensions, unit weights, and mechanical properties must comply with the strict parameters defined in Table 2 for each designation. For example, designation '15.2-1860-P' must maintain a nominal diameter of 15.2 mm, a nominal area of 139 mm², a nominal mass of 1086 g/m (with a ±2% tolerance), a minimum breaking load of 259 kN, and a minimum 0.2% proof load of 228 kN.

To verify structural uniformity, lay length is measured on a horizontal sample using plain and carbon paper. Carbon paper is rubbed gently over the strand to leave wire impressions. Vertical lines are drawn at the start and end of 6 consecutive wire impressions, and the distance is measured. The test must be repeated at three different places, and the average taken as the length of lay.

Nominal mass is evaluated by cutting a 100 cm sample, measuring its mass in kg, measuring the exact length of the centre core wire in metres, and calculating nominal mass per unit length (kg/m) as the ratio of sample mass to core wire length.

The total elongation under load must be at least 3.5 percent on a minimum gauge length of 600 mm. An initial load equal to 10% of the minimum breaking load is applied, a suitable extensometer is attached and adjusted to 0.001 mm/mm, load is increased to 1.0% extension, the extensometer is removed, and tension is continued until a wire breaks to calculate final elongation.
When the finished strand is cut with a disc cutter, the individual wires must not unravel, or they must be capable of being easily repositioned back into place without difficulty.

To prevent premature notches, cuts, or bends from gripping jaws (which lead to test errors), the length of the grip must be at least equal to one lay length and must distribute the load uniformly. If hot-dip tinning or socketing with material is used for sample preparation, temperatures must be carefully controlled and kept below 370 °C to prevent heat degradation of strength and ductility.

Representative samples for breaking load, proof load, and elongation tests must be cut from one end of a random coil selected from every group of 5 coils, with a minimum sample size of at least 2 from each lot.

If it is equal to or greater than the rejection number, the lot is rejected. If it falls between the two, a second sample of equivalent size is tested. The cumulative defectives are compared to the second acceptance/rejection thresholds to determine final lot conformity.

requirements: Every tower bolt conforming to this standard may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards.
Stainless steel tower bolts must be manufactured in five standard nominal sizes: 100, 150, 200, 250, and 300 mm. The size of the tower bolt is designated by the length of the barrel (B).
The stainless steel sheet utilized for forming the barrel must conform to Grade X07Cr18Ni9 or Grade X10Cr17Mn6Ni4N20 of IS 6911.
The stainless steel sliding bolt itself must conform to Grade X04Cr13, Grade X12Cr13, Grade X04Cr18Ni10, or Grade X07Cr18Ni9 of IS 6527.

To prevent screw head protrusions and ensure flush installation, all tower bolts made from sheet steel thickness of 0.70 mm and above must feature countersunk screw holes suitable for countersunk head wood screws (conforming to IS 6760).

The sliding bolt must be of robust, single-piece construction with an integral knob. Alternatively, the knob may be securely fitted via a pin, or screwed and riveted to the bolt, designed with round profiles and zero sharp edges.

Dimensions must satisfy: a) Width of barrel (C) must be 33 mm (for 10.0 mm diameter bolts) or 38 mm (for 12.0 mm diameter bolts); b) Sliding bolt diameter (D) must be minimum 10.0 mm, or 12.0 mm; c) Length of the socket (E) must be minimum 25 mm.

Dimensional clearance limits mandate: a) Thickness of steel sheet for barrel (F) must be minimum 0.7 mm (for 10.0 mm bolts) or 1.0 mm (for 12.0 mm bolts); b) Bore diameter of the barrel or socket (G) must be between 0.7 to 1.5 mm larger than the actual sliding bolt diameter (D) to ensure smooth mechanical sliding action.

The minimum number of equally spaced screw holes in the barrel and sockets (for wood screw No. 6) is strictly sized: 6 holes (for size 100), 8 holes (for size 150), 10 holes (for sizes 200 and 250), and 12 holes (for size 300).

Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the finished tower bolts must be polished bright with a smooth, defect-free surface. If requested by the buyer, the finished hardware must undergo mutually agreed corrosion resistance testing.
Each finished tower bolt must be clearly and legibly marked with the manufacturer's name, brand/trade-mark, and the words 'Stainless Steel' imprinted onto the metal surface.

A lot comprises all identical tower bolts of the same size manufactured in a single day. Random samples must be selected and tested per Table 2: a) Up to 200 bolts (sample size 5, allowed defectives = 0); b) 201 to 300 (sample size 8, allowed defectives = 1); c) 301 to 500 (sample size 13, allowed defectives = 2); d) 501 to 800 (sample size 20, allowed defectives = 2); e) 801 and above (sample size 25, allowed defectives = 3).

Under the 'Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Aluminium Composite Panels manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). requirements: Every panel must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly and indelibly on its reverse face or secure label, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17682).

The composite panel must consist of three main structural layers: a top and a bottom coated aluminium sheet, and an in-between core layer made either of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) or mineral-based fire-retardant material, bonded together using high-performance adhesive films.
Panels are classified into six distinct application grades to match structural and fire demands: Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 2S, Grade 3, Grade 4, and Grade 5.

The standard specifies three nominal size configurations: a) 1 200 mm × 2 400 mm; b) 1 200 mm × 3 050 mm; c) 1 200 mm × 3 660 mm. The nominal sheet thicknesses are 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm, 5 mm, and 6 mm. Other dimensions can be mutually agreed between manufacturer and buyer.

Finished panel dimensions must satisfy: Length tolerance of +4 mm, width tolerance of +2 mm. Thickness tolerances: less than 3 mm is ±0.1 mm; 3 mm and above is ±0.2 mm. Edge straightness deviation must not exceed ±0.5 percent (tested per Annex C), and squareness deviation is limited to a maximum of ±5 mm (tested per Annex C).
Manufacturers must verify raw materials: polymer granules (Clause 5.1), aluminium alloy sheets (Clause 5.2), and surface coating parameters (Clause 5.4).

Finished panels must satisfy physical-mechanical limits: core polymer density, aluminium sheet tensile strength, yield strength, elongation, and joint T-peel strength (testing adhesive bond integrity between the core and aluminium sheets).

Coatings must undergo strict quality audits: dry coating thickness, cross-cut adhesion, pencil hardness, specular gloss, color/gloss retention, and accelerated weathering under the updated weathering test IS 101 (Part 6/Sec 5) [1].

For fire-retardant panels (Grade FR), the composite assembly must undergo fire testing to verify: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) to check combustion limits, Smoke Density Rating to measure toxic fumes, Ignitability, and Surface Flame Spread behavior.
When requested by the specifier, panels must pass optional engineering tests to certify Sound Transmission Class (STC) ratings, sound absorption coefficients, and thermal conductivity coefficients.

High-carbon steel chemical constituents must be verified via ladle analysis: Carbon limits, Manganese, and restricted maximum Sulphur and Phosphorus content (restricted to <= 0.040 percent each) to prevent brittleness.

requirements: For static cantilever testing, the butt end of the full-size pole must be rigidly clamped from the base up to the ground line inside a standardized concrete crib layout to simulate real-world ground embedment.
The lateral load must be applied at a constant, continuous rate to cause deflection at the point of load of N cm/min, calculated using the formula: N = 0.00015 * L^2 * Cg.
Under the rate of deflection formula, 'N' represents the deflection rate in cm/min, 'L' is the lever arm distance in cm, and 'Cg' is the circumference at the ground line in cm.
The pulling steel cable must be secured tightly around the pole at the designated load point, equipped with inline dynamometers or load cells to record lateral tension during pulling.

The maximum fibre stress at the ground line (F) must be calculated using the equation: F = (P * l) / Z, where P is load at failure in kg, l iscorrected lever arm in cm, and Z is the section modulus (Gg^3 / (32 * pi^2)) using ground-line circumference.

If a pole fractures at a point other than the ground line, the fibre stress at break (Fb) is calculated using the equation: Fb = (P * l1) / Zb, where l1 is distance from break to point of load in cm, and Zb is (Gb^3 / (32 * pi^2)) using break circumference.
Requires recording all natural defects (knots, checks, shakes, splits, and taper) before testing to evaluate their structural influence on strength and stress limits.
The test report must record the cross-section dimensions at five critical points: ground line, load point, top end, butt end, and break point.

Because timber strength varies significantly with moisture, the moisture content of the pole at the time of testing must be determined on small clear specimens cut from the pole using standardized oven drying.

All observed or calculated physical dimensions, deflection values, and stresses must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

requirements: The direct shear test must utilize a standard square brass or gunmetal shear box (conforming to IS 11229) with nominal dimensions of 60 mm x 60 mm x 50 mm, split horizontally at mid-height.

For undrained tests, solid or plain toothed grid plates must be positioned over the specimen to prevent drainage. For drained tests, perforated grid plates and porous stones must be placed at the top and bottom of the specimen.
Testing requires an air-dried soil sample (nominally 1 kg) passing through a 4.75 mm IS sieve, compacted into the shear box in three equal layers using a standardized hand tamper.

Predetermined normal vertical stress is applied to the specimen via a top pressure pad and loading yoke. For drained tests, the specimen must be allowed to consolidate fully under this vertical load before shearing.

Before commencing horizontal shear, the vertical clamping pins holding the box halves together must be removed, and the separation screws adjusted to create a slight gap to prevent metal-on-metal friction during sliding.

During a consolidated drained (CD) test, the horizontal shear displacement must be applied at an extremely slow, constant rate of strain (derived from consolidation curves) to guarantee that at least 95% of excess pore water pressures are dissipated.

The horizontal shear force is applied continuously and recorded using a calibrated proving ring, with readings taken until the shear stress peaks and declines, or horizontal displacement exceeds 20% of the specimen length.

To determine the true shear stress at failure, the shear force must be divided by the corrected contact area, as the horizontal overlapping area of the split box halves decreases continuously during shear.
Under the October 2009 amendment, the corrected area calculation is updated to the geometrically correct formula: Ac = Ao * ((6 - δ) / 6), replacing a historical printing typo in the original code.

The test must be repeated on separate specimens at a minimum of three (preferably four) different vertical normal stresses. The peak shear stress values are plotted against normal stresses to draw the Mohr-Coulomb failure envelope, where the intercept is cohesion (c) and the slope is the angle of internal friction (φ).

Final observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match those of the specified limits.

requirements: Every certified door handle/knob and its packaging box must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the CM/L licence number.
Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 8.1 (a) is modified to require that each individual door handle be clearly and indelibly marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade mark'.

Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 9.1 (a) is modified to require that each packaging carton be marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade name', while the previous packaging marking requirement under Clause 9.1 (b) is completely deleted.
Covers two main types: a) Lever door handles; b) Door knobs.
Handles must withstand high pulling forces (tested using axial strength apparatus with tension loads up to 1000 N) without stripping threads, breaking, or pulling loose from the spindle.

The spring return mechanism must withstand high durability cyclic testing (up to 200,000 operations depending on durability grade) with zero structural failures, loss of return angle, or spring slippage.
Handles must withstand neutral salt spray testing (up to 240 hours depending on grade) to ensure corrosion resistance on finishes (plated, painted, or anodised layers).

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the statutory 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Fire Retardant Plywood must conform to IS 5509 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified fire-retardant plywood is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to processed wood panel products.
requirements: Every fire-retardant plywood sheet must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 5509).

In cases where fire-retardant chemical treatment is applied at the veneer stage and finally after the manufacture of the plywood, the plywood so produced must conform strictly to the BWR (Boiling Water Resistant) grade of IS 303.
Chemical treatment may be executed either by pressure impregnation after manufacture or by soaking of plywood/veneer. If veneer treatment is chosen, it must be performed using the soaking method.
Thickness deviations of the finished panels must satisfy strict limits: a) Less than 6 mm allows ±10 percent; b) 6 mm and above allows ±5 percent.

The straightness of edges and ends of plywood must be verified against a straight edge of at least the full length of the panel. The maximum gap (convex or concave) must not exceed 2 mm per 1 000 mm (0.2 percent).

Squareness of the plywood must be checked with a 1 200 mm × 1 200 mm square by applying one arm of the square to the plywood edge and measuring the maximum gap, which must not exceed 2 mm per 1 000 mm (0.2 percent).
To retard rapid combustion, the panel must undergo standard flammability evaluations. The time taken for the second ignition of the specimen under standard flame exposure must be at least 30 minutes.
To slow thermal breakthrough, the flame penetration time through the panel thickness must be not less than 15 minutes for every 6 mm of thickness.
The time taken to lose weight from 30 percent to 70 percent under standard burning exposure must be not less than 20 minutes.
The finished plywood must be reasonably clean to handle and completely free of dirt and stains, other than a uniform surface color resulting from the flame-retardant chemical solution.
Lot grouping and statistical sampling must be drawn randomly in accordance with the specifications of IS 7638.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Door Fittings (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all hydraulically regulated floor springs must conform to IS 6315:2025 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified floor springs in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial builders hardware.
requirements: Every certified floor spring body must be legibly and indelibly marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and classification code.
When tested, the floor spring must meet all mechanical and safety requirements in accordance with its declared classification code (similar to the 6-digit coding of IS 3564).

For floor springs featuring adjustable closing force, the unit must be capable of adjustment at least to power size 3, and the manufacturer must provide precise, clear instructions to the installer to ensure correct setup.

If a floor spring has adjustable power sizes, two floor springs must be drawn from the lot for durability and efficiency testing: one unit is set to the minimum power size and the other to the maximum power size.

Floor springs are tested on assemblies to verify closing moment, opening moment, and efficiency. For double-action floor springs, the direction of closing must be alternated between clockwise and anticlockwise directions after every 5,000 cycles.

Fire-rated floor springs, when installed as per instructions, must be capable of closing the test door from any angle to which it may be opened. One sample must be tested on door assemblies in accordance with IS 3614.

One floor spring is subjected to salt spray testing. The opening and closing forces of the floor spring are measured before and after salt spray exposure (and subsequent post-rinsing) to verify that corrosion does not impair functional operation.

The opening and closing forces are measured slowly (not faster than 1°/s) using a force gauge positioned perpendicular to the door face from 0° to 4° and 88° to 92° (taking the average of three readings). The efficiency of the floor spring is calculated as:
Efficiency = (Average of maximum closing force between 0° and 4°) / (Average of maximum opening force between 0° and 4°) * 100.
This efficiency must not be less than the values defined in Table 1 for that power size.
For doors with latches, the closing speed must be regulated so that the door smoothly engages with the latch. The closing time shall be easily adjustable between 5 seconds and 20 seconds.
If provided with a back-check function, the floor spring must be capable of hydraulically stopping or cushioning the test door before it reaches a 90° open position.

If delayed closing is provided, the closing time from 90° to the end of the delay zone must not be less than 20 seconds at an ambient temperature of (25 ± 5)°C. The delay zone must not extend beyond the 65° open position, and the manual override torque must not exceed 150 Nm. After 500 test cycles, the delay time must remain between 10 s and 30 s.

Floor springs must be packed in individual packs and suitably reinforced to prevent physical damage. Packaging must be designed to protect the contents from moisture and physical handling during storage and transport.
